message:
test(update): pin the enumeration trap the three-tier case is built to avoid

Test 1. No product change. Three checks added to the three-tier section of 8fc93d5, on the
reviewer's warning.

fixture_children filters on `t.parentPid == parentPid`, which is one level. The leaf's parent is
the middle, so a three-tier test enumerating that way hands PrepareForSwap a set that does not
contain the process the test is about -- and then passes, having exercised nothing. The section
already followed parentage instead, and that was the whole of the defence: a comment and a
helper nobody was required to use.

Now the trap is a check. One-level enumeration is run alongside the chain walk and asserted to
find two of the three, with the leaf missing; the chain walk is asserted to find it. Anyone who
swaps the enumeration back gets a failure that names the reason.

The third check is the ordering the walk depends on -- each tier started before the one below
it. Without it a fixture whose creation times did not line up would be exercising the rejection
path while appearing to test acceptance, which is the same class of quiet pass.

46 checks, three runs clean.
